overview: Liechtenstein is a tiny landlocked country in the Alps, between Switzerland and Austria. Its capital is Vaduz. Liechtenstein is a principality, ruled by a prince, and it uses the Swiss franc as its currency. It has had no army since the 1860s. Despite its small size, it has one of the highest incomes per person in the world.

geography.text: Liechtenstein is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world: it is surrounded only by other landlocked countries. Its western part lies in the flat valley of the Rhine, which forms the border with Switzerland, while the east rises steeply into the Alps.
